notes: Known-answer navigation tasks for the typescript lane. Needle-based, not line-based: bench/verify-tasks/verify.mjs resolves every needle to a unique line at the current SHA, so the manifest survives edits without stale line numbers. Paths are relative to the lane root (typescript/), not to the repository root. 'expect' blocks carry the ground truth a harness scores against; counts are minimums where marked (min_symbols, min_incoming) and exact everywhere else. On implementation and cardinality tasks exact_count counts concrete, non-generic, unconditionally compiled types that satisfy the contract directly or through inheritance, plus, on card-rule-contract only, the structural rule values that nominal_count and structural_count describe; abstract bases, blanket impls and cfg-gated impls are excluded. On an implementation or cardinality list, optional_sites names declarations that satisfy the contract but are not counted: the abstract classes that implement or extend it, directly or through another abstract class, and the interfaces that extend it; a tool may return them or not. Every implementations entry and optional site is anchored on the line that carries the declared name of the class, interface or rule value, even where its heritage clause continues on the lines below; a concrete class that reaches the contract by two paths (an abstract base and an extending interface) is listed and counted once, and a value that only holds implementors, such as a registry array, is not an implementor. card-rule-contract splits its exact_count in two: nominal_count counts the classes whose declaration carries `implements RuleContract`, structural_count the exported object literals that name the contract only through a `: RuleContract` annotation or a `satisfies RuleContract` clause (a value that merely has the shape is not counted), and the two sum to exact_count. On a multi-parent task the list holds the direct parents named in the anchored declaration's heritage clauses, one per name and never a further ancestor: extends_count counts the names in its extends clause, implements_count those in its implements clause, and exact_count, where a task states it, counts all of them, so it equals extends_count plus implements_count whenever both are stated. references exact_count counts lines, not occurrences, over every .ts and .tsx file under packages/ (sources and tests): a line counts once when the asked name is written on it as an identifier that refers to the anchored declaration, however many times, which takes in calls, reads, constructions, type positions, JSX tags, decorators and every import, import type or re-export line that binds the name (in a multi-line import or export list, the line that carries the name); the from line, the name of any declaration (the namespace half of a class + namespace merge included), comments and docblocks, string literals and module specifiers never count. On a name_only task the string literal is the name: every line outside comments that carries it counts, the from line excepted. repeated_sites names a needle that keys `lines` identical lines of one file, each a separate site under that rule, so exact_count is the known_sites plus every repeated line. On a references list optional_sites names lines that link to the name without carrying it (on the name_only task, the lines that only import or re-export the constant holding the literal); a tool may return them or not, and they are never counted. packages/bench/tests/referenceCounts.test.ts recounts every references task under this rule. On a definition task that names no target file, exact_count counts every overload signature declared for the called name, each a known_site, never the implementation, which the candidate anchors; on a declaration_merge task it counts the declarations that merge into the merged name (the qualifier when from.symbol is a member), each a known_site. known_sites holds file+needle lines whose role the surface sets: the counted sites on references, the counted declarations on a definition or declaration_merge task with exact_count, two of the four counted names on imp-glob-import (the other two are must_include names), and, on a task with a target and no count, lines an answer may return beside the target, which are neither required nor counted. min_incoming is a floor on distinct callers (a function, method or test callback whose body holds at least one call to the anchored method), not on call sites; each incoming_includes entry is one call-site line inside a caller it lists. Kinds added by the fifth wave: jsx_element (a capitalised JSX tag, which resolves to the component function of that name), jsx_factory (an intrinsic lowercase JSX tag, which is a call to the factory h that jsxFactory configures), ambient (a global declaration in a .d.ts script with no import or export: a namespace, or a `declare const` the build defines), ambient_module (a declare module block in a .d.ts that stands in for a package no file provides), paths_alias (an import specifier rewritten by a tsconfig paths entry, such as @app/* to packages/app/src/*). document_symbol tasks count every named symbol the anchored FILE declares (types, members, functions, constants); each task's note enumerates that count N and states min_symbols = floor(0.75 * N), the 25% margin absorbing listings that fold container nodes. A named symbol is one of the file's module-level declarations (a class, interface, enum, type alias, namespace, function, variable or constant) or a member one of them declares (a property, method, accessor, constructor, interface or enum member, and each constructor parameter property, which declares a member); function-local variables, parameters, object-literal keys, anonymous callbacks, and import or re-export bindings (`export * as` included, which creates no name inside the file) are not symbols; a namespace is one symbol and the declarations inside it are not counted (neither document_symbol file declares one with members, and the recount fails if one does). symbols lists every counted name, one entry per declaration, and packages/bench/tests/documentSymbols.test.ts recounts both tasks under this rule. call_hierarchy tasks name callees under outgoing_includes and callers under incoming_includes; both are file+needle pairs the verifier resolves. Kinds added by wave 2: same_name (two exported symbols carry one name in two modules, so the module path decides and the name cannot), name_only (a string literal is the only link between two sites because nothing declares it as a symbol), glob (an all-names edge, `export * from`, which re-exports every name its target module exports; exact_count on this surface counts those names and is a lane-specific fact, not a cross-lane one). Other kinds this lane uses: barrel (a named import from the @atelier/core package root, whose index.ts holds only export ... from lines: following it must reach the declaring module and must not fan out to the other modules the index re-exports), declaration_merge (one name declared twice in one scope, an enum plus a namespace, a class plus an interface, or two interfaces, which TypeScript merges into one symbol: the name resolves to both declarations, a member resolves to the half that declares it, and the merge is never an inheritance edge), namespace_import (import * as Rules from "../rules" gives one object holding every export; only the members this file reads, here Rules.RULES, are edges, so the import must not expand to the whole module), shadow_alias (two modules each export a class called Formatter, and state.ts imports both under renames, Formatter as MoneyFormatter and Formatter as StatusFormatter: a type written with the rename resolves to the class in the module its import specifier names), structural (a value that satisfies an interface by shape alone: no implements clause names the interface, so the link is reached only through type compatibility, never through an implements or extends edge), syntax_error (a deliberately broken .ts fixture, an unclosed class body or unbalanced generics, that tsconfig excludes from the build: the expected parse result is an error, never a recovered tree), type_only (an import type, or a name used only in type positions, which is erased at compile time: the edge is type-level only and is never a runtime dependency). Kinds shared with other lanes, worded identically in every lane that uses them. child_of: the anchored declaration is the child end of a parent edge, and the answer is a direct parent it extends, implements or embeds, one level up, never a further ancestor and never one of its own children. imports: an import that binds only the names it lists; the answer is each named declaration in the file that declares it, never a sibling declared beside it and never every name the target module exports. lane_local: a symbol every lane carries under the same name or as its lane equivalent (Money, Customer, Dataset, the reference prefix, the invoice calculator's calculate, the billing Formatter); resolution must land on this lane's own declaration and never cross into a sibling lane. parent_of: a parent edge scored for direction, with the anchor at either end; the parent is the type that is extended, implemented or embedded, the child is the type that does so, and an answer that reports the child as the parent is wrong. uses_self: a type that refers to itself, such as a tree node holding children of its own type; the edge is a uses edge back to the declaring type, never extends, implements or embedding. from.symbol is the identifier a task asks about, exactly as written on the from line and with no qualifier: the alias where an alias is used, the member on a member access, null when the question has no single identifier. from.occurrence (1-based) says which one when it appears more than once on that line, and is then required. document_symbol, parse-negative and diagnostics tasks ask about a file and carry neither key.
